rationale: C06 plausibly supplied a material policy-and-drafting template for the child. Both committee letters address a rule that would automatically cut off United States economic or financial assistance when an aid recipient exports specified goods to the Soviet bloc. C06 develops the central rationale later applied to the Netherlands: a rigid cutoff can weaken a strategically important friendly nation more than the Soviet bloc, while selective, cooperative export controls better protect United States security. The child adapts that framework to the Battle Act's waiver mechanism, adds transaction-specific facts, evaluates the Netherlands' defense contribution and export controls, and formally determines that aid should continue. C25 and C19 are strong secondary structural analogues because they use the recurring committee-letter sequence of factual predicate, strategic-security findings, statutory determination, and aid action, but their Yugoslav assistance decisions concern materially different statutory machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Any shipment of any such items listed automatically results in all military, economic and financial assistance to the Netherlands being cut off, unless I determine ... that "cessation of aid would clearly be detrimental to the security of the United States."
shared_material.parent_excerpt: [The amendment] would require the United States to cut off economic and financial assistance to all countries which export to the Soviet Union or its satellites any articles which might be used for the production of military materiel.
shared_material.explanation: The documents address the same concrete cutoff mechanism: exports to the Soviet bloc triggering termination of United States assistance.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Technical experts in this country believe that this amount of this particular type of equipment would not add significantly to the capacity of the Soviet bloc to explore for, or to produce petroleum.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Before legislation of this character is adopted, we ought to be sure that we would get more out of it than we would lose.
shared_material.explanation: The child particularizes C06's proportionality rationale by finding that the shipment made no significant contribution to Soviet-bloc capacity.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Cessation of aid to the Netherlands would materially weaken the whole system of defenses now being built up under the North Atlantic Treaty.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it would weaken the free nations more than it would weaken the Soviet bloc.
shared_material.explanation: This is the central shared security rationale against an automatic aid cutoff.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Netherlands Government cooperates with the United States and other countries of the free world to prevent or limit drastically export to the Soviet bloc of items that are considered to be strategic.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The appropriate agencies of the Government have been negotiating ... with countries receiving aid from us in order to curb trade that would aid the war potential of the Soviet bloc ... This method, which permits selective and cooperative treatment ... is far superior to the arbitrary blanket approach
shared_material.explanation: Both rely on cooperative, selective export controls as the preferred administrative mechanism.
